I'm afraid that if I open up, I'll be seen as a drain on their resources or a distraction from their own challenges.

I've been living with chronic pain for over a decade now, and it feels like it's only getting worse. I've tried various treatments, but nothing seems to provide long-term relief. I've been struggling to keep up with my work, family, and social obligations, and the lack of sleep only makes things worse. I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, and it's exhausting.

I've been taking care of my elderly mother for the past couple of years, bringing her groceries and doing her laundry every week. I dread these visits, feeling guilty for my emotions towards her, even though I love her deeply.

Yes, I've been dealing with a lot of stress lately due to work and personal issues. My father passed away a few months ago, and I've been struggling to come to terms with his loss. I've tried some relaxation techniques before, but they haven't seemed to make a difference. I'm open to trying new approaches and working with you to find a solution.

I've never really felt lonely or isolated, even as a caregiver. I've always had my family and friends around me, and they've been incredibly supportive. I've always felt like an outsider, even in my own family. I've attempted to contact her several times, but she's been unresponsive. I'm worried that my attempts to communicate may only make things worse. My brother has always been protective of her, and I fear that involving him in our conversation might escalate the situation.

I'm not confident that this process is the right approach for me. I've always been a simple person, and I trust that when it comes time to make a decision, I'll make the right one. I don't anticipate my kids objecting to my decision-making style, as they've always trusted my judgment.

I've been struggling with feelings of sadness and hopelessness for months now. I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy, and I find myself withdrawing from my friends and family. I can't seem to shake these feelings no matter what I do.

My anxiety has reached a point where it is interfering with almost every aspect of my life. I struggle with excessive worry and fear, frequently imagining worst-case scenarios. Through counseling, I want to find ways to reduce my anxiety and regain a sense of stability.

I've been caring for my mom for the past ten years, and I've come to realize that I've been minimizing the impact it has on my life. I've been feeling like I'm not doing enough, that I'm not being a good daughter, and that I'm neglecting my own needs. But hearing you acknowledge the importance of my role and the emotional weight it carries has given me a renewed sense of purpose.

I've been dealing with [Health Condition] for as long as I can remember, but it's been particularly bad since my husband was diagnosed with a chronic condition. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, and I can't focus on anything else. I've tried various coping mechanisms, but nothing seems to work for very long.

I've been trying to balance my job, my family, and my own mental health, but it's all becoming too much. I feel like I'm failing him, and I can't bear the thought of him being alone in a nursing home.

A constant feeling of sadness and lingering emptiness consumes me daily, leaving little room for positive emotions. Thoughts of unworthiness and self-criticism spiral out of control, and it's as though happiness has become an unattainable concept.

One significant event that triggered these emotions was the sudden end of a long-term friendship. The loss amplified existing insecurities and loneliness, pushing me into this depressive state. Additionally, stressful work environments and lack of fulfillment contribute to my overall dissatisfaction with life.

These depressive symptoms persist almost every day, affecting my ability to concentrate and carry out tasks efficiently. They reflect upon my relationships, causing social withdrawal due to fears of rejection and burdening others.

While occasional distractions like engaging in creative hobbies provide momentary relief, understanding what therapy can offer and learning about specific approaches to combating depression would be greatly appreciated.

I frequently experience intense panic attacks that leave me completely shaken. It starts with a racing heart and shortness of breath, followed by a overwhelming sense of fear and impending doom. These episodes can happen anywhere - at home, work, or even in public places - making it difficult to feel safe and secure. I avoid certain situations or places out of fear of triggering these panic attacks. The constant worry about when the next one will strike is exhausting and debilitating. I want to learn how to manage these overwhelming moments of anxiety and regain control over my life. Can you guide me on techniques or coping mechanisms to help prevent and reduce the frequency of these panic attacks?

The pressures of juggling multiple responsibilities, such as work, family obligations, and financial burdens, have left me feeling stretched thin. I often feel overwhelmed, irritable, and emotionally drained. Physical symptoms like headaches and stomachaches have become more frequent too. To navigate through this stressful period, I would like to learn healthier ways to manage stress, set boundaries, and create self-care routines. What strategies can we explore during our counseling sessions?

I've been feeling increasingly isolated from my friends and family lately. I've tried reaching out, but it feels like no one has the time or energy for me. I've been haunted by my mother's illness for months now. The memories of her hospitalization and the countless procedures she's undergone have left me feeling helpless and powerless. I've been feeling extremely down and empty for months on end. No matter how hard I try, I can't shake off this overwhelming sense of sadness. My goal for this counseling session is to better understand my depression and explore potential treatment options. I often catch myself ruminating over negative thoughts about myself, my future, and finding joy in anything. It feels like I'm losing interest in activities that used to bring me pleasure. The triggers for my depressive episodes seem to vary, but lately, stress at work and conflicts with family members have been major contributors. These feelings of despair usually persist throughout the day, every day, and they have lasted for more than six months now. How can I start the process of healing from this depression?

"My marriage feels stagnant after years of being together."
 The patient hopes to reinvigorate their marriage and find ways to strengthen the bond they share with their partner.
Emotions and thoughts: The patient expresses feelings of boredom, complacency, and dissatisfaction in their marriage. They yearn for more excitement and emotional connection.
Triggering event: The patient noticed a decline in intimacy and passion over the past few years. They believe the routines of daily life and other obligations have contributed to this shift.
Symptoms: The patient experiences sadness and frustration about the state of their marriage regularly. Feelings of loneliness and hopelessness arise when contemplating the future of their relationship.
Life events/family dynamics: The patient's parents divorced when they were young, making them especially determined to work through challenges rather than repeat the cycle of failed relationships.
Coping strategies: The patient initiated open conversations with their spouse about their concerns and has considered seeking therapy as a couple.
Question: How can we bring back the spark in our marriage? Are there any specific exercises or activities that could help enhance emotional intimacy?

I've been feeling overwhelmed by my daily responsibilities, especially those related to caring for my mother. I've always felt like I've been the caretaker in my family, and I've never really had anyone to turn to when I needed help. I've always put everyone else's needs before my own, and I've come to realize that I've been doing it for so long that I don't even know what I want or need anymore.

I've been struggling with feelings of hopelessness and helplessness for years. I've always felt that I'm not good enough, no matter what I achieve. Stress seems to control every aspect of my life at the moment. Not only do I feel overwhelmed by work demands, but I'm also dealing with personal challenges within my family. I've been dealing with feelings of anxiety and apprehension since my mother was admitted to the hospital. I've been caught in the middle of a family conflict for the past two and a half months. My siblings and I have been meeting weekly to sort out our mother's estate, but the real reason for their cooperation might not be as altruistic as it seems.

I've been feeling so disconnected from myself and the world around me. I've lost touch with the things that once brought me joy, and I feel like I'm just going through the motions of life. I've tried to reach out to friends and family, but I can't seem to connect with them in the same way I used to. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of sadness and loneliness.

I've thought about that, but I don't have the resources to hire someone or ask for help from family. My siblings live far away, and I can't burden them with this responsibility. I've been trying to manage everything on my own since my mother passed away last year.

I've been feeling overwhelmed with the demands of my job and the responsibilities at home. My husband's health issues have added to my stress, and I've been having trouble sleeping and focusing on my work. I feel like I'm constantly running on empty.

I've been dealing with severe anxiety lately. It feels like an overbearing sense of fear that grips me and makes it difficult to breathe. In therapy, I hope to uncover the root causes of my anxiety and develop strategies to calm myself in those moments.

I've been struggling with anxiety and stress when it comes to discussing financial matters with my family member. These conversations often result in heated arguments, leaving me feeling drained and helpless. I've tried to avoid them altogether, but I know that can't be a long-term solution. I've even considered just giving in to their demands, but that doesn't feel right either. I've always prided myself on being a good communicator, but I feel at a loss when it comes to this issue.

I've been a caregiver for most of my life, taking care of my mom and later my husband. The weight of their needs has left me feeling drained and neglected. I've come to realize that I've been neglecting my own self-care, and I'd like to change that. However, the thought of entrusting my mom's care to new caregivers fills me with anxiety. I've had negative experiences in the past, and I'm hesitant to trust again.

I've been feeling really down lately, and I hope to achieve a sense of happiness and fulfillment in my life through this counseling session. My emotions are constantly shifting between sadness, emptiness, and worthlessness. It feels like there's a black cloud hanging over me all the time. Certain triggers have worsened these feelings, such as losing my job recently due to company downsizing. I also find it difficult to sleep at night, often waking up feeling fatigued. These symptoms have been persistent for about six months now. In terms of significant life events, I experienced the loss of a loved one last year, which has contributed to my current state. Whenever I feel overwhelmed, I tend to isolate myself from friends and family, which further exacerbates my feelings of loneliness.

My mother has been battling cancer for years, and lately, she's been struggling to express her pain. I've tried to be there for her, but I can't help but feel helpless when she can't articulate her suffering. I've noticed that she's been withdrawing from me, and I fear that her condition is worsening. I've tried to discuss this with her, but she becomes agitated and dismissive, which only adds to my anxiety. I feel like I'm failing her as a daughter and a caregiver.

Anxiety has been interfering with my ability to enjoy the present moment. Even during moments of relaxation or leisure activities, my mind is constantly racing with worries and what-ifs. It's exhausting to never fully be able to switch off and just be in the moment. I'm hopeful that counseling can help me cultivate mindfulness and find peace amidst the chaos.

My marriage has been going through a rough patch lately and it's causing me a lot of distress. I feel disconnected from my spouse and the spark we once had seems to have disappeared. In this counseling session, I want to explore ways to improve our communication and reignite the love in our marriage.

I've been feeling quite isolated lately, but I was fortunate to have two neighbors who have special needs children. I've tried reaching out to local support groups, but I've found it difficult to connect with others due to my busy schedule and the stigma surrounding mental health. (Sharing personal history)
Growing up, I was always the last to adopt new technologies. My parents were early adopters, and they'd often scold me for being behind the times. I remember feeling embarrassed and left out when my classmates had the latest gadgets, and I couldn't afford them. My wife's itching has been a persistent issue for months, and no matter what I try, I can't seem to alleviate her discomfort. I've been hesitant to bring this up with her healthcare provider, fearing that they may not have any new solutions to offer. The emotional toll of watching my wife suffer is immense, and I feel helpless in the face of her pain.

My spouse and I have been married for several years, but lately, we've been growing apart. We hardly spend time together anymore, and when we do, it feels like we're just going through the motions. I miss the deep connection we used to have, and I'm worried about the future of our relationship. Are there any strategies or exercises we can try to reignite the spark and strengthen our bond?

I've been taking care of my mother for years, but her needs have become too great for the caregiving company to handle. She's very stubborn and doesn't want help with showering or other personal care. I've considered getting more help, but it would mean going beyond the current caregiving outfit.

My anxiety often leads to excessive rumination and overthinking. I find myself replaying past conversations or events in my mind, analyzing every detail and searching for potential mistakes or embarrassing moments. This constant self-criticism takes a toll on my mental well-being.

I've been struggling to find the motivation to travel with my husband due to my grief over losing my parents. I've tried visualizing our trip to Niagara Falls, but it doesn't seem to help. I feel like I'm stuck in the middle of an ongoing family conflict, and it's taking a toll on my emotional well-being. I've been keeping my husband's illness a secret from my kids, fearing that it would negatively impact our relationship and their emotional wellbeing. I've tried to maintain a normal family life, but I can't help feeling guilty for not being completely honest with them.

I was surprised when my cat jumped onto my mom's lap for the first time in a long while. The sight of it purring contentedly on her lap brought a sense of peace to the room. It was a stark reminder of the bond we once shared as a family. I've missed that connection, and it's been a long time since I've felt so close to anyone.

The memories of my childhood home are bittersweet. My mom and I used to spend hours sitting together, petting the cats and sharing stories. But as the years passed, the dynamics in our family changed. My sister moved in, and the balance shifted. I felt like an outsider in my own home.

The thought of introducing my sister to the cat is a complex issue. On one hand, I want to protect my mom and the bond we share. On the other hand, I don't want to create unnecessary conflict or tension. I've tried to bring it up with my mom, but the conversation always ends in tears and hurt feelings.

Lately, I've been feeling really disconnected from my friends and family. It's like we're drifting apart, and I don't know how to bridge that gap. I miss the deep conversations and the support system we used to have. I understand that relationships change over time, but it feels like I'm losing important connections in my life. How can I nurture and strengthen my existing relationships so that they remain meaningful and fulfilling?

My anxiety has become so overwhelming that it's affecting my ability to maintain healthy relationships. I constantly worry about what others think of me, fearing judgment or rejection. This fear often leads me to avoid social situations altogether, isolating myself from friends and family. I don't want my anxiety to dictate my social interactions anymore, and I hope counseling can help me overcome this hurdle.

I've been having trouble sleeping since my husband's deployment was announced. Every night, I find myself lying awake, replaying worst-case scenarios in my mind. I know it's irrational, but I can't help feeling that something terrible will happen to him.

I've been feeling a deep sense of sadness and loss lately. I've been thinking about my parents' aging process and the eventual loss of their independence. I've also been reflecting on my own mortality and the fear of losing control over my life.

I've been a caregiver for the past seven years, managing things for my husband who has Alzheimer's disease. It's been an incredibly challenging journey, filled with emotional ups and downs. I mentioned how I had a good friend, [Name], who helped me out by staying with him when I needed to run errands or take a break. But lately, I've been feeling overwhelmed and exhausted. I've been neglecting my own needs, and I've noticed that my health has started to suffer. I've been experiencing frequent headaches, insomnia, and a general lack of energy. I've also been feeling increasingly irritable and anxious, which I know is affecting my relationship with my husband and my family.

Good day, I'm looking for assistance in navigating through the emotional fallout caused by past trauma. Some traumatic events from my childhood have resurfaced, resulting in distressing flashbacks and nightmares that disrupt my sleep and affect my daily functioning.

One particular experience that significantly impacted me was witnessing a severe car accident as a young child. The images and sounds continue to haunt me to this day. Whenever I see or hear similar events depicted on the news or even in movies, it triggers intense anxiety and overwhelming emotions.

These symptoms occur frequently, and their intensity leaves me feeling emotionally drained, fearful, and vulnerable. They tend to last for hours, making it difficult to focus on tasks or engage with others. It feels as though I'm still stuck in that moment, reliving the terror over and over again.

I am interested in discussing therapeutic approaches that can help individuals recover from trauma. Are there specific techniques or treatments that you find effective? Additionally, how do you approach working with individuals who have experienced traumatic events? I am hopeful that counseling can provide guidance and support as I work towards healing from these painful experiences.

My husband, [Name], has no quality of life. He refuses to join us for meals or activities, leaving me feeling isolated and alone. I've tried talking to him about it, but he just shrugs me off. I've even considered leaving him, but I don't know if that would make things better or worse.

I've been giving my family member her pain medication as prescribed, and I'm not worried about addiction. She tells me her chest hurts, and I give her Metamucil, which seems to help. I've been feeling really low for a while, and I think counseling could help me understand and alleviate my depression. It's hard to pinpoint exactly what triggers these depressive episodes, but they seem to come out of nowhere and last for days or weeks at a time. During these periods, everything feels hopeless, and I struggle to find enjoyment in things I used to love.

One example of what triggered a recent episode was receiving negative feedback at work. Instead of taking it constructively, I spiraled into a pool of self-doubt, berating myself for not being good enough. These self-deprecating thoughts then snowballed, affecting my mood, energy levels, and motivation.

The frequency of these depressive episodes varies, but they occur approximately once or twice a month. Some days are more manageable than others, but the weight of sadness and lethargy often drains me. Basic tasks become arduous, and I withdraw from activities and relationships that once brought me joy.

In my family history, there is a significant presence of depression and mood disorders. While genetics may play a role, various life experiences such as traumatic events and chronic stress have also likely contributed to my vulnerability.

I want to explore ways to manage my depression, develop coping strategies for when these episodes occur, and work towards building a more fulfilling life. What treatment options would you recommend, and how can counseling help me navigate through this journey?

I've been struggling with the pressure I put on myself to meet unrealistic goals, despite having a full household with multiple family members and a grown child to take care of. I feel like I'm constantly falling behind and failing not only myself but my loved ones as well. I can't seem to find the balance between my personal aspirations and my family obligations.

Hello, Doctor. Lately, I've been on a journey of exploring spirituality and it has brought up a lot of questions and emotions within me. I grew up in a strict religious household, but as I've grown older, I've started questioning my beliefs and seeking a deeper understanding of spirituality. This search has caused conflicts with my family who strongly adhere to our traditional religious practices. I feel torn between honoring my family's expectations and following my own spiritual path. I'd like guidance in reconciling these conflicting feelings and finding a way to navigate spirituality in a more personal and authentic way.

I've been feeling more isolated and lonely since my husband's illness, particularly in terms of my social life. I used to play tennis and be part of a team, but now I work full-time at his office, which leaves me with less time for social activities. I still keep in touch with my friends through texting and group chats, but it's challenging to get together with them in person. Most of my college friends are spread out, and I only manage to see them once a year.

I've been feeling overwhelmed by the demands of my job and personal life lately. I've been working long hours and haven't had much time for myself or my family. I've been trying to manage my stress through exercise, but I've found myself skipping workouts due to my busy schedule. I've also been having trouble sleeping, which only adds to my exhaustion. I've tried reaching out to my friends for support, but I've felt like a burden, and I don't want to impose on them.

I just don't know how to handle my child's behavior anymore. It feels like everything I do is wrong and nothing works. These outbursts happen quite often and it leaves me feeling helpless and unsure of what to do next. The frequency of these tantrums has been increasing lately and they last for about an hour each time. I grew up in a strict household and sometimes find myself subconsciously using similar disciplinary methods, but they seem to be ineffective now. Could you provide guidance on positive discipline techniques that align with my values?

(deep breath) I've been feeling overwhelmed lately, and the thought of another session adds to my anxiety. I've been dealing with a lot of stress at work, and my personal life has been chaotic as well. My mom passed away last year, and I've been struggling to process her loss. I've been having nightmares and panic attacks, and I can't seem to focus on anything for long periods. I'm afraid that I won't be able to make progress in our sessions if I can't even keep my thoughts together during the day.

I've been feeling trapped and powerless in my situation, unsure of how to navigate the complex web of relationships and expectations. I've tried to communicate openly with my husband and family members, but it seems that no matter what I do, I'm unable to make everyone happy. I'm starting to feel like I'm at a crossroads, and I'm not sure which direction to take.

I've been taking care of my mother for years now, and it feels like an endless cycle. I'm exhausted, and I can't keep doing this alone. My siblings don't seem to care, and I can't help but feel angry and bitter about it.

Hello doctor. Lately, I've been wrestling with a profound sense of sadness and disinterest in life, and I'm seeking guidance on how to overcome my depression. One event that aggravated my depressive symptoms occurred during a family gathering last month. While everyone laughed and engaged in conversations, I couldn't find any motivation to participate. Instead, I silently observed from a distance, feeling detached from the joy around me. Additionally, my energy levels are incredibly low, making even basic tasks feel exhausting. Concentration is a struggle, and my self-esteem has taken a significant blow, leading to excessive self-criticism. Are there any therapeutic techniques you recommend to help lift this heavy cloud of depression?

I've been thinking about it, and I believe setting a goal to prioritize my time and energy could be a good first step. I've realized that I often take on too much, and it's important for me to learn to say no to things that don't align with my values or that I can't handle effectively. I'd also like to work on managing my anxiety in the moment, rather than letting it spiral out of control.

I've been torn between two options. The first is to sell our house and move into a smaller, more affordable place, which would allow us to focus on my husband's health without worrying about the mortgage. The second option is to stay in our current home, which would provide stability for our children and allow my husband to receive treatment in a familiar environment.

I appreciate your perspective, counselor. I've been thinking about how I can best support my sister without imposing my own judgment on her decisions. I remember reading about the concept of unconditional positive regard in counseling psychology, and I believe that approach could be beneficial in this situation. I'll try to focus on understanding her perspective and providing her with accurate information, rather than trying to control her choices.

Ever since I moved to a new city, my stress levels have skyrocketed. I don't have any close friends or family here, and it's been challenging to adjust. I worry about how I come across to others and if they will accept me. Additionally, I've noticed that my sleep patterns have significantly changed. I struggle to fall asleep and often wake up in the middle of the night feeling restless and anxious. It's become a vicious cycle where lack of sleep contributes to even more stress. Coming to counseling, I hope to explore ways to manage these feelings of stress and loneliness.

My brother, [Name], has always been prone to angry outbursts. But lately, it seems like things have gotten worse. He's started wearing a thick, woolen coat whenever he feels his temper rising. It's not just the coat that's concerning me; it's the intensity of his anger and the frequency of these outbursts.

I've noticed that I've developed some destructive habits, such as excessive drinking and engaging in reckless behaviors when I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed. My friends and family are concerned about my well-being, and deep down, I know that I need to change these patterns. Through counseling, I want to understand the root causes of my behavior and learn healthier coping mechanisms.

I've been feeling a deep sense of sadness lately, as I've come to terms with the fact that my mother won't be around forever. I've been cherishing our time together and expressing my gratitude towards her, but it's bittersweet knowing that these moments are limited. I can't help but feel a sense of loss, even though she's still here with me.

I have been feeling down and unmotivated for several months now, and it's starting to affect my daily life. My goal for this counseling session is to understand what may be causing my depression and find strategies to overcome it. I often feel overwhelmed with sadness and hopelessness, and I struggle to find enjoyment in activities that used to bring me happiness.

Recently, the loss of a loved one has triggered a significant decline in my mood. The grief feels all-consuming at times, and I find it challenging to navigate through daily tasks. Additionally, I have faced some relationship difficulties which have contributed to my feelings of isolation and despair.

Although I have tried various coping mechanisms, such as journaling and exercise, they haven't been effective in alleviating my depressive symptoms.

I would like to know more about the therapeutic process and how counseling can help me address my depression. What treatment options do you suggest, and what approach do you take to counseling individuals with depression?

(sighs deeply) I feel so overwhelmed. I've been taking care of Mom for years, and now that she needs more help, I can't seem to get it right. I'm worried about her safety, but my sisters keep questioning my decisions. I feel like I'm failing her.

The conflict between my siblings and me has reached a breaking point. We can't seem to get along anymore, and it's affecting our entire family. I want to find a way to mend these broken relationships and create a more harmonious environment.

I've been dealing with chronic pain for over a year now, and it's been taking a toll on my emotional wellbeing. I've tried various pain management techniques, but nothing seems to work consistently. I've been feeling helpless and frustrated, and I'm worried that my family might grow tired of my constant complaints. I'd like to find a way to manage my pain effectively while also maintaining healthy relationships with my loved ones.

I've been struggling with the issue of my mother's dementia and her constant need for security due to her past experiences. Her paranoia about people taking things and hiding them has been escalating, and it's become a significant problem. I've tried to manage from a distance, but it's become clear that she needs more help than I can provide. She's had a fall since moving into assisted living, and she's received a full neuro-workup. I'm feeling overwhelmed and unsure of how to proceed.

Over the past few years, I have experienced several significant losses in my life, including the death of a close family member and the end of a long-term relationship. These events have left me feeling deeply saddened and hopeless at times. It's challenging to process these losses and move forward.

I've been wrestling with the dilemma of leaving my stable job to pursue a career that I'm passionate about, but the thought of jeopardizing my financial security and my ability to care for my aging parents leaves me feeling trapped and anxious.

My goal for this counseling session is to strengthen my marriage. Lately, my spouse and I have been experiencing constant arguments and lack of emotional connection. I want to identify the underlying issues and learn effective communication techniques to rebuild and maintain a healthy relationship.

Being a parent has become more challenging than I anticipated, and I would like some guidance on how to navigate the ups and downs of parenting. My stress levels have reached a new high, especially due to recent financial difficulties. I constantly worry about making ends meet and providing for my family. Every bill that comes in feels like a weight on my shoulders. I need guidance on how to handle this overwhelming stress.

I've been feeling overwhelmed lately. My family member's illness has taken a toll on me, and I've been struggling to keep up with their care while also managing my own responsibilities. I hope to find ways to honor his memory and eventually move towards acceptance and healing.

These past few months have been incredibly stressful for me, resulting in feelings of overwhelm and exhaustion. Today, my goal is to seek advice on coping strategies to manage stress more effectively. I've been dealing with feelings of anxiety and depression for years, stemming from a difficult childhood and a series of traumatic experiences. Hi, I am seeking counseling because stress has taken a toll on my life, and I want to learn how to manage it effectively. My goal is to find ways to reduce stress and regain control over my well-being.

To address my stress levels, I've tried relaxation techniques such as deep breathing exercises, but they only bring momentary relief. Are there more effective tools you could suggest for managing stress? Can therapy help me identify any underlying factors contributing to my stress?

I've been struggling with my role as a caregiver for my terminally ill husband. I've been feeling overwhelmed and unsure of how to balance my own needs with his. I've been trying to keep up with his medical appointments, manage his medications, and provide emotional support, all while dealing with my own grief and anxiety.

I've been dealing with feelings of worthlessness since my mother passed away two years ago. I've been living with my brother and his roommates since then, and they've been incredibly supportive.  My dad has started showing signs of forgetfulness and confusion more frequently. He often misplaces items or forgets important events and appointments.
